**An experiment needs a decision rule before the results are visible.** Define the primary outcome, diagnostic metrics, guardrails, and integrity checks. The primary outcome answers the main product question; diagnostics explain mechanisms; guardrails limit unacceptable harm; invariants check whether the experiment ran correctly. [1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.04922)

For a recommender, qualified engagement might be primary, coverage and clicks diagnostic, complaints and latency guardrails, and assignment/logging consistency invariants. Specify exposure unit, duration, useful effect size, and stopping rules.

**A positive p-value result is not an automatic launch decision.** A statistically detectable gain can be too small to matter, accompanied by a failed guardrail, or invalidated by sample-ratio mismatch. Repeated looks and many tested metrics also affect inference.

Inspect confidence intervals and practical tradeoffs. Investigate instrumentation or assignment failures before rerunning, and do not discard inconvenient metrics after seeing them. Ship when the evidence supports the intended causal claim and the complete product outcome is acceptable. The experiment's job is to inform that decision, not merely produce one favorable number.

**Technical details and references.**

Define one primary outcome tied to the decision, diagnostics that explain changes, guardrails limiting harm, and invariants checking experiment integrity. For a recommender, these might be qualified engagement, click/coverage breakdowns, complaints/latency, and allocation or logging consistency respectively. State exposure unit, duration, minimum effect, and stopping rules before launch. [1](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.04922)

A statistically positive primary metric does not justify launch if a prespecified safety/quality guardrail fails, sample-ratio mismatch invalidates assignment, or instrumentation is broken. Distinguish confidence intervals from practical importance and account for repeated looks or multiple comparisons. Diagnose failures before rerunning; do not discard inconvenient metrics after seeing results. Ship only when the experiment supports the intended causal claim and the total product tradeoff is acceptable.
